# Anticipating Data Policy in the Age of AI

[Blog](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7476882733634613248/)by Stefaan Verhulst and Adam Zable: “The world’s relationship to data is changing rapidly. Artificial intelligence has generated significant excitement for its potential to help solve public problems, improve decision-making, and create new forms of economic and social value. At the same time, it has intensified longstanding debates around access, ownership, attribution, privacy, labor rights, security, and the responsible reuse of public-interest data. Questions that once sat at the margins of data policy have moved to the center.

Governments, international organizations, civil society groups, and companies are responding with a growing range of governance approaches, from executive orders and regulatory frameworks to international agreements, industry standards, and new institutional models. Yet it remains difficult to distinguish short-term developments from deeper structural shifts. While discussion often focuses on the latest AI breakthrough, the more important question for policymakers is how these technologies are reshaping the systems, assumptions, and governance models that determine how data is accessed, shared, and used.

To better understand these changes, The GovLab convened two forecasting studios bringing together experts working in data governance, digital policy, open science, AI governance, and public-sector innovation. Participants explored emerging trends in data access, governance, and reuse, examined the forces driving those trends, and considered what they may mean for the future of open data and public-interest data ecosystems.

The discussions identified seven signals that point to significant changes already underway. These signals suggest that the future of data governance will be shaped by advances in AI alongside evolving expectations around trust, stewardship, infrastructure, sovereignty, reciprocity, and public value. They offer a starting point for understanding how data policy may need to evolve in the years ahead. A longer version of this analysis, with a full list of studio participants and more detailed discussion of each signal, will be published separately…([More](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7476882733634613248/))”.

# 預判 AI 時代的資料政策

Stefaan Verhulst 與 Adam Zable 在[部落格文章](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7476882733634613248/)中寫道：「世界與資料之間的關係正在快速改變。人工智慧因其有潛力協助解決公共問題、改善決策，並創造新的經濟與社會價值，而引發高度期待。與此同時，它也加劇了圍繞取得、所有權、歸屬、隱私、勞動權益、安全，以及負責任再利用公益資料等長期爭論。過去位於資料政策邊緣的問題，如今已移到核心位置。

各國政府、國際組織、公民社會團體與企業，正以愈來愈多元的治理方法回應，從行政命令與監管框架，到國際協議、產業標準與新的制度模式皆然。然而，要區分短期發展與更深層的結構性轉變，仍然並不容易。討論經常聚焦在最新的 AI 突破，但對政策制定者而言，更重要的問題是：這些技術如何重塑那些決定資料如何被取得、分享與使用的系統、假設與治理模式。

為了更深入理解這些變化，The GovLab 召開了兩場預測工作坊，邀集從事資料治理、數位政策、開放科學、AI 治理與公部門創新的專家參與。與會者探討資料取得、治理與再利用的新興趨勢，檢視推動這些趨勢的力量，並思考它們對開放資料與公益資料生態系未來可能代表的意義。

討論辨識出七項訊號，指出重大變化已經正在發生。這些訊號顯示，資料治理的未來將受到 AI 進展，以及圍繞信任、託管、基礎設施、主權、互惠與公共價值等不斷演變的期待共同形塑。它們提供了一個起點，協助理解未來幾年資料政策可能需要如何演進。此分析的較長版本，包括完整的工作坊參與者名單，以及對各項訊號更詳細的討論，將另行發布……（[更多](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7476882733634613248/)）」。
